short: Bounded scalar curvature and Ricci flow

title.title: Does bounded scalar curvature keep Ricci flow alive?
title.subtitle: Claim: yes in dimension 4, where the flow extends; no in high dimensions, where it can still blow up

plain: In 4D, one simple number tells you if a shape-smoothing flow will break; in higher dimensions it can lie

beats.text: Schematically: watch the scalar curvature $R$ as the flow runs toward time $T$
A flow can only stop when the full curvature $|\mathrm{Rm}|$ blows up
Claim: in dimension 4 bounded $R$ rules that out; in high dimensions it does not

steps: Suppose the flow stops while the scalar curvature stays bounded
Zooming in would show a Ricci-flat 'bubble' carrying the blow-up
In dimension 4 no such bubble exists: the flow goes on

achievement.label: The scalar-curvature extension question
achievement.note: Dimension 4 rests on a companion inequality on Ricci-flat trees

verify.detail: No Lean: 118 pages across three papers
verify.ourCheck: We read the papers' strategy; we did not check the proofs

voice.text: The flow stops only when curvature blows up. Is the scalar part enough to watch?
A blow-up with bounded scalar curvature needs a bubble; four dimensions forbids it.
Claimed: yes in four, no in high dimensions.

sources.quote: (i) A smooth Ricci flow on a closed 4-manifold with uniformly bounded scalar curvature on [0,T) extends smoothly past T. (ii) In some dimension (q >= 10 parameter), a closed Ricci flow has bounded scalar curvature but unbounded full curvature at a finite singular time
Ricci flow can only stop when curvature blows up; is it enough to watch the scalar curvature?
118 pages across three papers; the 4d theorem relies on the companion tree inequality
